'''Alain Haché''' (born 1970) is an [[experimental physics|experimental]] [[physicist]], a [[professor]] at the [[Université de Moncton|University of Moncton]], Canada.<ref name="UMoncton" /> From 2003 to 2013 he held the [[Canada Research Chair]] in [[photonics]].<ref name="njUvf" /> He is also the author of ''The Physics of Hockey'' <ref name="vuzVX" /> and ''Slap Shot Science'',<ref name="bYPKd" /> two [[popular science]] books on [[ice hockey]].

Haché was born in [[Tracadie, New Brunswick]] in 1970.{{cn|date=March 2022}} In 2002, he and undergraduate student Louis Poirier transmitted [[faster-than-light]] electrical pulses through a 120-metre long "[[photonic crystal]]" made of [[coaxial cable]]s of alternating [[characteristic impedance]] (12 pairs of 50&nbsp;[[ohm|Ω]] and 75&nbsp;Ω cables).<ref name="U41Mr" /><ref name="AXuse" /> The experiment showed that the pulse envelope was recreated at the end of the cables at a speed of >3&nbsp;[[speed of light|''c'']]. This speed represents the [[group velocity]], but the amplitude of the signal also drops in such a way that the energy transmitted never exceeds, at any given time, the energy that would have been transmitted by same pulse travelling in a vacuum.
